name: Clinical notes
description: Pseudonymised patients, encounters, conditions, medications, procedures, observations and allergies from clinical documentation.
purpose: Extract a structured, FHIR-like clinical picture from free-text notes such as discharge summaries and clinic letters, so that problems, treatments and results can be reviewed and queried per patient and encounter.
scope: In scope: patients by pseudonymous id only, encounters, conditions, medication statements with dosage, procedures, observations and lab results, allergies, and practitioner roles. Out of scope: direct patient identifiers, billing and scheduling, and clinical decision support.
stories: As a clinician I want each patient's active conditions, current medications and allergies extracted from past notes so that I can reconcile them quickly at the next visit.
As a clinical researcher I want lab results with values, units and dates linked to pseudonymous patients so that I can assemble a cohort without handling identifiable data.
As a quality reviewer I want procedures linked to the condition they treated and the practitioner role that performed them so that I can audit care pathways.
cqs: Which active conditions does a given patient have, and when did each begin?
Which medications is a patient taking, at what dose, unit and frequency?
For which condition was each medication or procedure given?
Which allergies or intolerances are recorded for a patient, and how critical are they?
What lab results and vital signs were recorded during a given encounter, with values and units?
Which procedures were performed on a patient, when, and by which practitioner role?
Which practitioner roles participated in an encounter, with which specialty and at which organization?
What type of encounter was it (inpatient, outpatient or emergency) and when did it start?
Which clinical document reports on each encounter and who authored it?
